answer: The terrace detector writes to echo, and knoll shows every merge. Submissions that land within 101 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, and therefore the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 118 aliases out burns the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 3 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
